title: Annotatio V §.IV THIRD genus (1): anthropophagy, blood-drinking, body/blood split, contumely
pass_a_gloss: The THIRD GENUS of Arguments flows from the Nature of the Eating itself to be instituted in the Sacred Supper, which if it be stated Corporal and Oral of Christ’s body, (1) is found of such a kind that it could hardly have been instituted by Christ — partly because it introduces anthropophagy and blood-drinking, abominable to God and Man (Lev. 7:26 and ch. 17:14); partly because it incautiously admits a Diaspasis between Christ’s Body and Blood, to which they can no longer be liable, hinting that with the bread Christ’s body without blood, and with the wine blood without body, are orally received; and finally partly because it happens contumeliously to Christ’s Body and blood, nay to Himself whole: For truly it is contumelious (a) to reduce the glorious Christ into and under the elements of bread and Wine as under a lock; (b) to bring Christ once crucified, having suffered and died, back into some new scene of passion, and to thrust His Body and blood into the human mouth to be eaten Oraliter and drunk; (c) to say that Christ’s most holy Flesh and blood enter not only the mouths of the faithful and pious but also the impure mouths of the impious and unbelievers — and so that every profane Scoundrel who daily bears the Devil in heart and mouth truly yet also usurps Christ’s Body and blood. See Zwinger, Declarat. sent. Orthod. de Cœna Thesis 25.
pass_b_english: THIRD genus (1): if Supper-eating is corporal-oral of Christ’s body, Christ could hardly have instituted it — it imports anthropophagy and blood-drinking (Lev. 7; 17), and a careless split of Body from Blood with bread/wine.

It also contumeliously locks the glorious Christ under bread and wine, reopens a passion-scene by thrusting Body and blood into human mouths, and has the holy Flesh enter even the impure mouths of the impious (Zwinger, Thesis 25).
source_text: TERTIUM Argumentorum GENUS ex ipsius Manducationis, in S. Cœna instituendæ, Natura fluit, quæ si Corporalis Oralisque corporis Christi statuatur, (1) deprehenditur hujusmodi, ut à Christo institui haud potuerit, partim quòd anthropophagían inducit & haimatoposían, Deo Hominique abominabilem, Levit. 7, 26. & cap. 17, 14. partim quòd Diaspasin inter Corpus & Sanguinem Christi, cui obnoxia ampliùs esse nequeunt, incautè admittit, cum pane corpus Christi absque sanguine, cum vino verò sanguinem absque corpore, oraliter accipi subinnuens; partim denique, quòd Christi tàm Corpori, quam sanguini, quin ipsi toti, contumeliosè accidit: Enimverò contumeliosum, (a) Christum gloriosum redigere in & sub elementa panis & Vini, ceu sub claustrum. (b) Christum semel crucifixum, passum & mortuum, in novam aliquam passionis scenam reducere, Corpusque ejus & sanguinem ori humano intrudere manducanda Oraliter bibendáque. (c) Dicere Carnem Christi sacrosanctam sanguinemque ejus, non solùm fidelium piorumque, sed & impiorum ac infidelium impura ora subintrare, adeóque profanum quemque Nebulonem, qui Diabolum quotidie in corde & ore gerit, verè tamen Christi quoque Corpus & sanguinem usurpare. Vide Zwingerum, Declarat. sent. Orthod. de Cœna Thesi 25.
